plain.en: a fixed point we measure from

means.en: The fixed point from which we describe where something is. It is also called the origin.

plain.en: where an object is, measured from the reference point

means.en: Position is the distance and the direction of an object from the reference point at one instant. On a straight line, the sign + or - shows the direction.

plain.en: a change of position with time

means.en: An object is in motion if its position from the reference point changes with time.

plain.en: not changing position

means.en: An object is at rest if its position from the reference point does not change with time. Rest and motion depend on the reference point we choose.

plain.en: one exact moment of time

means.en: An instant is a single moment, with no length of time. We say the position at an instant.

plain.en: the time between two instants

means.en: A time interval is the time that passes from one instant to a later instant.

plain.en: the total length of the path an object covers

means.en: Distance counts every metre of the path, even if the object turns back. It has no direction.

plain.en: the straight change in position, with direction

means.en: Displacement joins the start point to the end point and has a direction. It is zero when the object ends where it started.

plain.en: size

means.en: The magnitude of a quantity is its size, without the direction. For example, 40 m is the magnitude of a displacement of 40 m to the right.

plain.en: total distance divided by total time

means.en: Average speed is the total distance travelled divided by the total time taken. It has no direction.

plain.en: speed with direction

means.en: Velocity tells how fast the position changes and in which direction. It is displacement divided by time.

plain.en: displacement divided by time taken

means.en: Average velocity is the displacement divided by the time interval. It can be zero even when the speed is not zero.

plain.en: motion with equal change in position in equal times

means.en: In uniform motion the velocity stays the same. The object covers equal displacements in equal time intervals.

plain.en: motion in which the velocity changes

means.en: In non-uniform motion the velocity changes, so the object covers unequal displacements in equal time intervals.

plain.en: the meter that shows a vehicle's speed

means.en: A speedometer shows, very nearly, the speed of the vehicle at that instant.

plain.en: how quickly the velocity changes

means.en: Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time taken. Its unit is m/s squared.

plain.en: a push or a pull

means.en: A force is a push or a pull on an object. It can change the speed, the direction or the shape of an object.

plain.en: a graph of position against time

means.en: A position-time graph has time on the X-axis and position on the Y-axis. Its slope gives the velocity.

plain.en: how steep a line is

means.en: The slope of a line is the rise divided by the run. On a position-time graph, it is the velocity.

plain.en: a graph of velocity against time

means.en: A velocity-time graph has time on the X-axis and velocity on the Y-axis. Its slope gives the acceleration and the area under it gives the displacement.

plain.en: equations that link velocity, time, acceleration and displacement

means.en: These equations work only when the acceleration is constant. They let us predict the motion.

plain.en: motion in a circle at constant speed

means.en: The speed stays the same but the direction keeps changing. So the velocity changes and the object is accelerating.

plain.en: the straight line that touches a circle at one point

means.en: In circular motion, the velocity at each point is along the tangent at that point.

plain.en: the sum of all the forces on an object

means.en: The net force is what is left after adding all the forces on an object, with their directions. The motion of the object depends only on the net force.

plain.en: forces that cancel each other

means.en: When the forces on an object are balanced, the net force is zero. Then the velocity does not change.

plain.en: forces that do not cancel

means.en: When the forces are unbalanced, a net force acts. The velocity of the object changes.

plain.en: the unit of force

means.en: The newton (symbol N) is the SI unit of force.

plain.en: the force with which the Earth pulls an object

means.en: Weight is a force, so it is measured in newtons. A spring balance measures it.

plain.en: a force that opposes sliding between two surfaces

means.en: Friction acts along the surfaces that touch, against the motion or the push. It can slow a moving object down.

plain.en: the push of a surface on an object resting on it

means.en: The normal force acts at right angles to the surface. For a box on a floor, it pushes the box up.

plain.en: the tendency of an object to keep its state of motion

means.en: An object at rest stays at rest, and a moving object keeps its velocity, unless a net force acts. This tendency is called inertia.

plain.en: the law about objects with no net force

means.en: If no net force acts, an object at rest stays at rest and a moving object keeps a constant velocity.

plain.en: the amount of matter in an object

means.en: Mass is measured in kilograms. For the same net force, an object with more mass has a smaller acceleration.

plain.en: the law linking net force, mass and acceleration

means.en: The acceleration is in the direction of the net force. It is proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to the mass.

plain.en: changing in the same ratio

means.en: If A is proportional to B, doubling B doubles A.

plain.en: changing in the opposite way

means.en: If A is inversely proportional to B, doubling B makes A half.

plain.en: mass multiplied by velocity

means.en: Momentum is the mass of an object multiplied by its velocity. It points in the direction of the velocity.

plain.en: the law about forces in pairs

means.en: When one object pushes on a second object, the second pushes back on the first with an equal force in the opposite direction.

plain.en: the objects we choose to look at together

means.en: We can take several objects as one system. Only the forces from outside the system change its motion.

plain.en: the pulling force in a stretched string

means.en: Tension is the force a stretched string or rope exerts on the objects it joins.

plain.en: a four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides

means.en: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. Its area is half the sum of the parallel sides, multiplied by the distance between them.
